content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Those who possess God-given spiritual discernment and therefore hear, obey, and faithfully respond to God, often contrasted with the foolish, disobedient, or unprepared.","primary_basis":["Proverbs 1:7; 9:10 — fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge and wisdom.","Psalm 111:10 — wisdom begins with fearing the Lord and is expressed in obedience.","Matthew 7:24–27 — the wise builder represents the person who hears Jesus’ words and acts on them.","Matthew 25:1–13 — the wise virgins represent readiness and faithful preparedness for the bridegroom’s coming.","James 3:13–17 — true wisdom is demonstrated by godly conduct and contrasted with earthly wisdom.","Daniel 12:3, 10 — the wise understand and remain faithful amid eschatological testing."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"In eschatological parables, the wise specifically symbolize the prepared and faithful people of God who are ready for Christ’s return, sometimes identified with the faithful church or remnant.","basis":["Matthew 24:45–47","Matthew 25:1–13","Daniel 12:3, 10"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The wise may denote faithful teachers, leaders, or interpreters who understand God’s purposes and guide others in righteousness.","basis":["Daniel 11:33, 35; 12:3","Matthew 24:45","Matthew 13:52"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"‘Wise’ can be ironic or negative, referring to those considered wise by worldly standards but who reject God and are exposed as foolish.","basis":["Isaiah 5:21","Jeremiah 8:8–9","Romans 1:22","1 Corinthians 1:18–29; 3:18–20"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"In some narrative interpretation, wise figures such as the Magi symbolize Gentiles or nations recognizing and worshipping Christ.","basis":["Matthew 2:1–12","Isaiah 60:1–6"],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad agreement about the positive biblical association of wisdom with fear of God, discernment, obedience, and preparedness. However, ‘wise’ is ordinarily a moral or spiritual description rather than a fixed symbol with one universal referent; its precise symbolic meaning depends on context."}
